questions.text: Quality of Service (QoS) Compliance: Adherence to standards: (1) Meeting regulator QoS targets (drop rate, success rate); (2) Payment of fines for non-compliance; (3) Reporting accuracy to regulator; (4) Spectrum license compliance; (5) Universal Service Fund contributions; (6) License renewal status; (7) Dispute resolution with regulator.
questions.evidence_required: QoS compliance reports, Fine payment receipts, License documents
questions.africa_specific_notes: Regulators frequently fine Telcos for poor service. Compliance is a license-to-operate issue.

questions.text: Competition & Anti-Trust Governance: Fair market conduct: (1) Dominance abuse prevention; (2) Fair interconnection rates; (3) Infrastructure sharing (tower co-location); (4) Mobile money interoperability compliance; (5) Pricing floor/ceiling adherence; (6) Mergers & Acquisitions compliance; (7) Agent exclusivity rules.
questions.evidence_required: Interconnection agreements, Pricing filings, Anti-trust audit reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Dominant players often accused of blocking competitors (e.g., agent exclusivity). Interoperability is a key regulatory push.

questions.text: SIM Swap Fraud Prevention: Protecting identity: (1) Strict identity verification for SIM replacement; (2) Biometric verification; (3) Notification to owner of swap attempt; (4) Cooling-off period for transactions after swap; (5) Internal staff monitoring (insider threat); (6) API security (for banks checking SIM status); (7) Victim compensation policy.
questions.evidence_required: SIM swap process docs, Fraud statistics, Audit logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: SIM swap is the #1 vector for financial fraud. Insiders often complicit. Banks rely on Telcos to stop this.

questions.text: Network Security & Data Protection: Defending infrastructure: (1) Signaling security (SS7/Diameter firewalls); (2) DDoS mitigation; (3) Customer data encryption; (4) Access control for engineers; (5) Vulnerability management; (6) Incident response plan; (7) ISO 27001 certification.
questions.evidence_required: Security audit reports, Penetration test results, ISO certificates
questions.africa_specific_notes: SS7 vulnerabilities allow tracking/intercepts. Data breaches can expose millions of users.

questions.text: AML/CFT Compliance (Mobile Money): Preventing financial crime: (1) KYC tiers (Tier 1, 2, 3 limits); (2) Transaction monitoring (suspicious activity reports); (3) Sanctions screening; (4) Agent due diligence; (5) Reporting to Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); (6) Staff training on AML; (7) Risk assessment.
questions.evidence_required: AML policy, Suspicious Activity Reports (stats), Audit reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Mobile money is a target for money laundering. Tiered KYC allows inclusion but requires monitoring.

questions.text: Float Management & Trust Accounts: Protecting user funds: (1) Separation of user funds from operational funds; (2) Trust account audits; (3) Interest distribution (if applicable); (4) Liquidity management (ensure agents have cash); (5) Insolvency protection; (6) Reconciliation frequency; (7) Insurance on float.
questions.evidence_required: Trust account statements, Audit letters, Liquidity reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: User funds must be 100% backed in trust accounts. If Telco fails, money must be safe.

questions.text: Board Oversight & Risk Management: Leadership accountability: (1) Board composition (independence); (2) Risk committee activity; (3) Audit committee independence; (4) Executive compensation transparency; (5) Whistleblower policy; (6) Anti-bribery/corruption policy; (7) Stakeholder engagement.
questions.evidence_required: Annual report, Board minutes, Risk register
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telcos are massive entities. Corruption in procurement or licensing is a risk.

questions.text: Supply Chain & Vendor Governance: Ethical sourcing: (1) Vendor code of conduct; (2) Local content requirements (procuring locally); (3) Modern slavery checks (hardware supply chain); (4) Bribery prevention in procurement; (5) Vendor performance management; (6) Diversity in supply chain; (7) Payment terms for SMEs.
questions.evidence_required: Vendor code, Procurement policy, Audit of suppliers
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telcos are major buyers. Late payment to local SME vendors is a common grievance.

scoring_notes: Layer 3 (Governance) for Telecom in SSA: SIM swap fraud and Mobile Money AML are the critical operational risks. Regulatory compliance determines survival.
